Amelia —

Appreciate the data. I took a quick pass and sketched a back-of-envelope unit-econ that maps to your sheet (attached). High-level:

- Baseline tokens per chat.reply: median ~ 1.2k tokens (prompt+response). summary.generate: ~450 tokens.
- With Redwood defaults (no quantization, standard prefix caching) the throughput/price tradeoff looks like ~0.012 USD per 1k tokens (hosted SKU baseline) which maps to ~0.014 USD/1k for your expected conversational mix with small bursts.
- Batching: recommend an adaptive micro-batch window of 12–20ms to capture short bursts — keeps p95 < 400ms for concurrency up to ~220 RPS per model shard in Dedicated. For hosted flows we typically configure small continuous-batching groups to balance latency and utilization.
- Caching: enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and common user fragments results in ~8–12% token reduction for you (we saw this in similar traffic profiles). TTLs at 600s are a good starting point; lowering to 300s increases cache churn and only marginally improves hit rate.

I attached karl's rough calc (karthik_unit_econ_sketch.xlsx) — it's intentionally simplified but shows sensitivity to tokens-per-call, cache-hit rate, and batching latency multiplier.

Next steps I propose:
1) PRD review with Novus infra to validate assumptions (this week)
2) Short eval run (7 days) with our eval harness to collect real tokens/use data
3) MAP signoff and procurement gating (target Wed 2029-04-17)

I'll loop Prio for runtime tuning and Ben for the procurement timeline.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference

Amelia,

A few implementation-level items that materially change units/dollars (we should lock these in the MAP):

- Quantization profile: moving to int8 quantization for your LLM variant reduces token CPU/GPU throughput cost by ~18% in our benchmarks with negligible quality degradation on summary.generate. We recommend a MUST-try during the 7-day eval.
- Prepend-level prefix caching: cache at the system prompt+recent-turns level for patient-identifiers; expect 6–10% token reduction.
- Batching policy: use a dual-tier policy — continuous micro-batching for low-latency paths (target 12ms), opportunistic macro-batching for non-interactive summary jobs (target 50–120ms). This keeps interactive p95 under 400ms and drops unit cost for bulk tasks.
- Failure fallback: configure automatic model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for >500ms latency spikes to preserve UX.

I'll prepare a short eval config (we call it 'novus-unit-econ-check') with these toggles and share the measurement spec (token buckets, per-route p95/p50, cache hit rate) tonight.

Cheers,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
